images.title: Sharing 9.5 kg of sugar
images.purpose: Show a decimal amount, 9.5 kg, shared equally into 4 bags so each bag holds 2.375 kg.
images.composition: One large sugar sack on the left, four equal bags in a neat row on the right joined to it by arrows, and one short equation line along the bottom; wide white margins.
exact_structure: Left: 1 large flat sugar sack filled teal #0072B2 with the tag 9.5 kg.
Right: exactly 4 identical smaller bags filled amber #E69F00, in one horizontal row, equally spaced, each with the tag 2.375 kg.
4 thin grey #6B7280 arrows, one from the sack to each bag.
Bottom centre: one line of text 9.5 ÷ 4 = 2.375 in dark text, with the decimal point of 2.375 coloured reddish purple #CC79A7.
No other objects, no people, no scale or shop background.
rejection: any bag tag other than 2.375 kg, or the sack tag other than 9.5 kg
images.takeaway: A decimal dividend is shared just like a counting number, and 4 bags of 2.375 kg make 9.5 kg again.
images.description: A sack labelled 9.5 kg with arrows to 4 equal bags each labelled 2.375 kg, and the line 9.5 ÷ 4 = 2.375.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on dividing a decimal by a counting number.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to check by adding 2.375 four times to get back 9.5 kg.

image_decisions.why: The equal sharing picture makes a decimal dividend divided by a counting number concrete.
